children: One of the biggest questions that emerged from the Nvidia crisis that spewed across Wall Street was the future of the tech company, or Nvidia after Jensen Huang, whether it is now or sometime later.
After his 'grand' return to the company, Huang has cleared the air on the topic of his succession.

While addressing his staff after his return, he discussed succession planning, a CNBC report said. He told staff that Nvidia had developed a team that did not need succession planning in the conventional sense, because its distinctive business model had several capable leaders overseeing different parts of the organisation.
A succession plan would add unnecessary hierarchy, Huang said, according to one person at the meeting.
In his address, Huang adopted a remorseful tone on Tuesday as he led his first employee meeting since being reinstated. He apologised for his actions and expressed regret.
NVIDIA CEO SAYS 'I HURT YOU ALL'

According to reports, the meeting was requested, and Huang, who asked to remain anonymous to discuss its details, told employees he had let them down and vowed to do better in his second stint. “I hurt all of you,” he said, one attendee recalled.
He further added that he had breached parts of the company’s code of conduct and made “some terrible mistakes”
During an hour-long all-hands meeting at Nvidia’s headquarters in Santa Clara, California, Huang addressed staff a day after resuming leadership of the company he co-founded three decades ago.
Huang also said he was in therapy and acknowledged that breaching aspects of Nvidia’s code of conduct was unacceptable.
He said the claim that he had been reinstated following pressure from US President Donald Trump on the board was false.

title: Nvidia doesn’t need a succession plan, says Jensen Huang after returning to company
